name: Mrk 42
observing_summary: Three consecutive nights in May 2025; 60–70 s exposures; ≈4 h per night.
reference_note: The star closest in brightness to the target was used as the statistical reference; the source text does not assign a fixed star number to that role.
validation_note: Comparison candidates were selected for brightness and isolation, checked against APASS DR9 and Gaia DR3, and known/suspected variables were excluded using VSX.
paper_title: The 2MIG isolated AGNs. 3. Optical–IR variability and dust reverberation in the NLSy1 galaxies Mrk 42 and Mrk 493

name: IC 5287
observing_summary: One 3.0 h sequence on 2025 June 30/July 1; 90 s exposures; 101 frames retained.
reference_note: Comparison star 1 was adopted as the primary statistical reference. The variability classification was unchanged when stars 2 or 3 were used instead.
validation_note: Three local comparison stars from APASS DR9; leave-one-out stability tests were applied. The adopted aperture minimized seeing dependence.
paper_title: The 2MIG isolated AGNs – 5. Hot-dust reverberation and spectroscopic constraints on BLR–dust scales in IC 5287 and Mrk 845

name: Mrk 845
observing_summary: Three consecutive nights in May 2025; ≈4 h per night; 112–125 frames retained after quality control.
reference_note: Primary statistical references: star 3 on 2025 May 20; star 4 on May 21 and 22.
validation_note: Four local APASS DR9 comparison stars; leave-one-out stability checks were applied. A common 9-pixel aperture was used on all three nights.
paper_title: The 2MIG isolated AGNs – 5. Hot-dust reverberation and spectroscopic constraints on BLR–dust scales in IC 5287 and Mrk 845
extra_note: APASS DR9 lists σV = 0.000 mag for star 4. This is not interpreted as a physically zero photometric uncertainty and is therefore shown here as unavailable.
